narration: The module starts from Q_map, the set of BEV query embeddings. Each query is one map element waiting to be refined.
Every query is fed to theta_offset, a learned projection that predicts where around the query the model should look.
Those predicted offsets are added to the reference points P_ref, so each query ends up with its own set of absolute sampling locations.
The resulting locations are used to sample the bird's-eye-view feature map F_bev, picking out a few cells instead of attending to the whole grid.
Bilinear sampling at those locations yields the sampled features, one feature vector per sampling point.
In parallel, the same queries pass through a small MLP that predicts a distribution rather than a fixed value.
The MLP outputs the mean and variance of a Gaussian, and dynamic resampling draws from that distribution at every forward pass.
The reparameterisation alpha_i equals mu_i plus sigma_i times epsilon turns the sample into the attention weight for each sampling point, keeping the step differentiable.
The sampled features are aggregated using those attention weights and the result is passed through a linear layer.
The output is delta Q_map, the residual update that is added back to the query embeddings to refine the map representation.
